source.title: Allspark: Weak to Strong Transfer via Alternating Chain of Thought
source.authors: Kai-Zhao Liang; Jun-Xiong Wang; Chen Liang; Zhen-Dong Wang; Qiang Liu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a trained weak model can improve a stronger model, but uses inference-time alternating reasoning rather than fine-tuning the strong student on weak labels, and reports accuracy rather than PGR. Its results therefore concern a related transfer method, not the specified versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports weak-teacher/strong-student accuracy comparisons and selected paired outcomes. These do not measure a strong student fine-tuned on weak labels, whether it beats the weak supervisor as a standalone model, or PGR. It also does not report a true-label-trained strong ceiling. Comparisons of Allspark with other teacher conditions are included where they report student accuracy; cited results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study does not fine-tune a strong student on a weaker model's labels. A weak teacher is trained with RL beside a frozen copy of itself. At inference it alternates chain-of-thought text with a frozen stronger student, and no weights change during transfer. No PGR, strong ceiling or weak-label training is measured. Burns et al. is cited and contrasted in related work. The results concern inference-time steering of a frozen model, a different construct from every version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The reader's 'tests/T2' contradicts its own finding that no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that an RL-trained weak teacher can steer frozen stronger students, within and across families, through alternating text reasoning, and that this improves accuracy–token tradeoffs on Inkling. They call the evidence initial and limited, and note that modeled dollar cost rises despite token savings (Appendix B.4).
record.recipe_differences: The strong student is not fine-tuned on weak labels. A weak teacher is trained with RL alongside a frozen copy of its initial model, then alternates text reasoning with a frozen strong student that produces the final answer. No PGR is calculated.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by student, domain, teacher condition and inference setting: Qwen3-4B Allspark transfer is approximately neutral in math and positive in reasoning; cross-family gains differ between Nemotron medium/full and Kimi. Inkling accuracy is evaluated across thinking-effort settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A weak teacher trained with RL beside its own frozen copy can raise the accuracy of frozen stronger students through alternating reasoning text. Gains: Inkling 81.6 vs 78.1; Nemotron +17.7/+5.2 pp; Kimi +11.5 pp. Effects are neutral or slightly negative for Qwen3-4B math (96.1 vs 96.9) and modest for reasoning (82.8 vs 81.2). Untrained and ordinary-RL teachers lower the 4B student's accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An RL-trained weak model can steer a frozen stronger model at inference via alternating chain-of-thought, with gains depending on student, task and inference setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected paired traces show steering helping, leaving answers unchanged, or harming the outcome (C4 shared indexing error).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual weak-teacher handoffs can help or mislead a frozen strong student; selected cases do not estimate rates.

record.problems: The authors describe the experiments as initial and limited in models, tasks and training runs. The Qwen comparison uses one training seed per method, and Qwen table entries have no uncertainty estimates. The Inkling and cross-family evaluations use 96 development tasks and three attempts per task; numeric bootstrap interval bounds are not given in the text. Development data were used for checkpoint selection in the Qwen study. The selected case studies are not aggregate evidence.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome rows were omitted. Figure 4 includes additional effort-sweep points, but the text does not give their individual numeric values; they are not separately extracted as figure-only rows.

untested.parts: No strong model is fine-tuned on weak labels; the student stays frozen and no PGR or true-label strong ceiling is reported.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensemble or loss variant for weak-label fine-tuning.
Model sizes, families and tasks vary only for alternating-CoT steering, not for PGR under weak-label fine-tuning.
No test of exploiting unverifiable errors, distribution shift, or shared-error effects on weak-label fine-tuning. The single C4 shared-error case concerns inference steering.
No theory of when a student must beat its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: Not a test of weak-to-strong generalization as defined by Burns et al.: there is no weak-label fine-tuning and no PGR. The Qwen study uses one seed per method, and development data were used for checkpoint selection. Table 4 checkpoint values and Table 8 cost estimates are not version-relevant and were correctly not extracted as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The strong student is frozen and receives alternating text reasoning, not fine-tuning on labels produced by the weak model. The paper does not report the weak supervisor's standalone accuracy for the relevant comparisons or calculate PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensemble of weak supervisors, or loss-variant comparison for weak-label fine-tuning is tested.
The paper varies model sizes, tasks, families and inference effort for its alternating-CoT method, but does not measure PGR or its predictors under the claim's weak-label fine-tuning procedure.
No test of exploiting what the supervisor cannot check, distribution shift, or whether shared errors reduce weak-label fine-tuning gains.
No theory of when a student must beat its supervisor is tested or developed.
